verdict.rationale: three.js runs directly in the browser via WebGLRenderer (default today) and has a WebGPURenderer with TSL shaders that work across both backends, giving a credible WebGPU migration path without rewriting shader code; the library ships as a lean core with optional addons (loaders, controls, SVG/CSS3D) keeping payload manageable, and huge adoption (12M+ weekly downloads) corroborates real-world browser deployment. missing for 10: no concrete payload/bundle-size benchmarks and no independent hands-on report specifically validating WebGPU production readiness/performance parity.
